svg.title: Q-101E-3: change bindings safely, then validate re-enablement
svg.desc: Identify all affected bindings. Disable or remove assignments bottom-up. An authorized parent change may proceed. Retained assignments stay disabled. Explicit enablement validates current relationships and authority. Failure leaves the assignment disabled; success permits enablement with continuing runtime checks. This differs from temporary ancestor-grant disablement.
svg.text: Q-101E-3 · Structural change and explicit re-enablement
Current rule: disabled bindings qualify; deletion is not mandatory.
1 · Discover all affected bindings and dependencies
Include branches, shared grants, actual parent teams and assignments.
2 · Disable OR remove affected assignments bottom-up
Handle the lowest dependent child first; stop where the change stops.
3 · Authorize and validate the structural parent change
Do not rewrite a parent beneath a remaining enabled binding.
4 · Retained assignments remain disabled
No automatic enablement, parent replacement, or authority copying.
5 · Explicit enable request: validate the CURRENT reality
Relationships · supporting assignments · grant validity · boundaries
Administrative authorization remains required; old support is not proof.
Invalid
Valid
Reject; assignment remains disabled
Unsupported lineage cannot authorize.
Assignment may be enabled
Runtime permission/scope/support checks continue.
Separate case: temporary GRANT disablement is not structural rewiring.
Disable G2 → still-enabled G3 is ineffective. Validly enable G2 → G3 can resume.
Explicitly disabled grants/assignments stay disabled. Orphaned authority remains ineffective.
